section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the theoretical and practical contributions of a study examining self-compassion as a protective factor against body image threats in young adult women. The findings reveal that within-person variations in self-compassion (state-level) provide benefits for affect, body image, and eating behaviors, independent of trait-level self-compassion. The authors emphasize that their within-persons approach offers broader implications than previous between-persons research, as all women can modulate their self-compassion on a daily basis.
